title: Klad lets an agent draw. A larger company needs a paid seat.
friendlyTitle: Klad lets an agent draw. A larger company has to pay.
summary: Klad is a drawing app built so a person and a coding agent can work on the same picture. The agent can add shapes, align them, and use a command-line interface. The file format, the command reference, and the agent skills are under the MIT license. The app itself is source-available under the PolyForm Internal Use License, not open source. A company with 500,000 euros or more in revenue in its last tax year needs a bought licence for each person who uses it.
friendlySummary: Klad is a drawing app a person and a coding agent can share. The agent can add and line up shapes from the command line. The file format and the agent instructions are free to reuse. The app itself is not open source. A company that made 500,000 euros or more last year needs a paid licence for each person who uses it.
whyItMatters: If you want an agent to draw, the useful split is the licence. Personal use, and use inside a smaller company, can be free. You may not redistribute the app. The drawings you make are yours, including brush settings copied into the file. There is no release build on the GitHub page yet. Read the licence before you put it on a company machine.
friendlyWhyItMatters: You can try it for personal work, or inside a smaller company, without paying. You cannot give the app to other people. The pictures you make are yours. There is no downloadable release on the project page yet. Read the licence before you install it at work.
